newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Consortium pledges $1 bln if wins Zambian mine bid.
newsitem.headline: Consortium pledges $1 bln if wins Zambian mine bid.

text.p: The Commonwealth Development Corp (CDC) said on Thursday that a consortium it was party to would spend $1 billion on developing Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) assets if it suceeded in buying them.

"The Kafue consortium would spend $1 billion on Zambian mines over the next five years. That would include the cost of buying them, and subsequent investment in them," CDC regional manager David Jones told an investment conference organised by the Financial Times.
The Kafue consortium comprises Avmin, Noranda, Phelps Dodge and CDC.
It is negotiating for the acquisition of ZCCM's Nkana and Nchanga divisions, the Chambishi cobalt plant and the Chingola refractory.

The Nchanga and Nkana divisions include five underground mines and one open pit mine, concentrator facilities, a tailings leach plant, a copper smelter and refinery, an acid plant and a cobalt plant. The Chambishi cobalt plant has a nominal capacity of 2,400 tonnes per annum.
Jones told Reuters later that the Kafue consortium and the Zambian government met on Wednesday to discuss unresolved details regarding the consortium's bid, but declined to give details.
"The two sides will hold another meeting next Monday," he added.
Asked to cofirm reports that the consortium's representaives walked out a recent meeting with government over sharp differences, Jones said: "We are continuing to negotiate".
